faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q5: Does the AI opt-out tag actually work?
faq.a5: For crawlers that respect it. yes. Major AI companies including OpenAI (GPTBot), Anthropic (ClaudeBot), and Common Crawl publicly commit to honouring ai:opt-out signals in image metadata. It is the metadata equivalent of robots.txt for AI training.
faq.q6: Does VeriMedia work on iPhone and Android photos?
faq.a6: Yes. Photos from iOS and Android are standard JPEG or HEIC files. VeriMedia processes both in-browser. HEIC files (iPhone default) are converted and shielded automatically.
faq.q7: What's the difference between Plus and Pro?
faq.a7: Plus ($9.99) unlocks batch shielding up to 100 files, 25 MB file limit, and creator profile metadata. Pro ($19.99.99) adds unlimited batches, 100 MB files, the Google Licensable Badge, and whitelabel mode.
faq.q1: Where do I find my license key?
faq.a1: After purchasing, check your email for the Paddle receipt. Your license key is the Transaction ID found in the receipt (it usually starts with txn_). Just copy and paste that into the Activation menu if it didn't activate automatically!
faq.q2: How do I block AI web crawlers from using my images?
faq.a2: VeriMedia embeds a standard "AI Opt-Out" tag (ai:opt-out = true) directly into your image file. This signals to major AI web crawlers (like GPTBot and ClaudeBot) that your work is off-limits for AI model training.
faq.q3: How do I add copyright info and licensable badges to my photos?
faq.a3: By embedding standard creator copyright links directly into the image files, search engines like Google can identify you as the author and display a "Licensable" badge next to your images in search results.
faq.q4: Why should I strip location metadata before uploading photos?
faq.a4: Hidden metadata inside raw photos contains your precise GPS coordinates, camera details, and dates. Stripping this data protects your location privacy and removes identifiers that bots can scrape.

privacy_page.intro: At VeriMedia.xyz, privacy is not just a feature - it is our absolute core value. Because this tool is engineered to help you strip invasive location tracking and camera serial numbers, we enforce a strict Zero-Data Collection Policy.
privacy_page.p1: VeriMedia operates entirely client-side. When you drop or upload a JPEG image into the sandbox, the file is parsed and modified in under 50ms using local browser APIs.
privacy_page.li1_1: No Uploads: Your images are never sent, uploaded, or transmitted to any external server or backend.
privacy_page.li1_2: Edge Computation: The EXIF purging, verified copyright injection, and AI opt-out tag (ai:opt-out=true) insertions happen strictly inside your browser's local sandbox memory cache.
privacy_page.p2: Because all computation is local, we maintain a complete vacuum of personal metadata:
privacy_page.li2_1: We do not store, view, or retain your uploaded photos or their metadata.
privacy_page.li2_2: We do not log coordinates, device models, or timestamp details.
privacy_page.li2_3: We do not maintain user profile databases, track user IPs, or record conversion metrics.
privacy_page.p3: If you choose to purchase Creator Pro:

privacy_page.li3_2: License Keys: When validating a license key, a secure request is dispatched directly from your browser to the payment processor. The status is cached locally.
privacy_page.p4: We do not deploy marketing trackers or invasive ad cookies.
privacy_page.p4_2: We use local storage only to remember your Pro activation status.
privacy_page.p5: We will never sell your non-existent data. Any structural updates will remain open-source and visible.

image_converter.faq_upload_a: Never. All decoding, conversion, and compression happen locally in your browser using the Canvas API and WebAssembly. The extension requests only the storage permission and makes no network calls during processing.
image_converter.faq_heic_q: How do I convert iPhone HEIC photos?
image_converter.faq_heic_a: Just drop them in. HEIC is the one format Chrome cannot decode natively, so we run a local WebAssembly decoder. Your photos are converted to JPG, PNG, WebP or AVIF entirely on your device, with correct orientation.
image_converter.faq_pdf_q: What can I do with PDFs?
image_converter.faq_pdf_a: You can convert PDF pages to images, combine images into a single PDF, compress a PDF at a chosen DPI and quality level, merge multiple PDFs, or split a multi-page PDF into individual page files. All of this is free.
image_converter.faq_pdf_size_q: Will PDF compression always reduce the file size?
image_converter.faq_pdf_size_a: Not always. PDFs that contain mostly text and vector graphics are already compact. Compression works best on PDFs with embedded photos or scanned images. The extension shows before and after size.
image_converter.faq_exif_a: EXIF metadata can include GPS coordinates, camera model, date taken, and more. Removing it protects your location privacy when sharing images. It applies when converting to JPG.
image_converter.faq_target_q: What is the max file size target?
image_converter.faq_target_a: A Pro feature that automatically finds the highest quality that fits under a size you set. It works for JPG, WebP, and AVIF.
image_converter.faq_sub_a: No. Pro is a single $7 payment that unlocks everything forever: unlimited batches, ZIP export, exact resize and crop, bulk rename, and max file size targeting.
image_converter.faq_activation_a: After purchase you get a license key on screen and by email. Paste it into the extension once. It then works offline.
image_converter.faq_refund_a: Yes, payments are handled by Paddle, our Merchant of Record. See our refund policy.
